column2: “I see.
So we've found the culprit, but now we don't know who the victim is.”
Toshio said with a snort.
“But isn't that strange?”
Mr. Kobayashi frowned.
“If the victim isn't Mr. Tanaka, where on earth did he come in from?”
“Through the front door, of course.”
“Impossible!{r}{p}A chime rings in the back whenever the door opens, so even if nobody was at the front desk, I couldn't have missed it.”
“That's true.
If he came in alone.{r}{p}But it's different if he came in with someone.{r}{p}...The victim came in together with Mr. Tanaka.”
“What on earth are you saying?{r}{p}That man was alone.
I'm certain.”
Mr. Kobayashi insisted, sounding angry.
“Did you check inside the ski bag?{r}{p}
...The victim was in there.{r}{p}Already dead, cut into pieces.”
All the girls gasped at once and covered their mouths as if holding back nausea.
“Then...
then the reason the body was cut up...”
{n2} said.
“Right,
it was to make it easier to carry.{r}{p}Besides, there's no way anyone could have cut a person up that much in such a short time.{r}{p}{n2},
do you remember that threatening letter?”
“Yes.”
He meant that scrap of paper the trio of girls had been making a fuss over.
“Judging from its wording, the culprit seems to have expected the body to be found around noon.{r}{p}Having it found too early was the culprit's biggest miscalculation.”
“Wait a minute.{r}{p}So the culprit left the body in the room, broke the window, and escaped from the second floor?”
“...Not quite.{r}{p}You don't need to break a window to escape from the second floor, do you?”
Everyone exchanged puzzled looks.
“Come to think of it, ya don't need to break the window at all...”
Mr. Kayama said, a hand on his chin.
“Breakin' in, sure, but gettin' out from the inside, ya just unlock it and that's that.{r}{p}So why'd he go and break the window?”
“To draw our attention.{r}{p}That sound told us something had happened, and as a result we all rushed to that room.{r}{p}The culprit deliberately made sure we'd find the body.”
“Why would he do that?”
{n2} asked the obvious question.
“...To make us misjudge the actual time of the crime and create an alibi.”
“An alibi?
But when the window broke, the culprit was still in that room, wasn't he?{r}{p}How could he have an alibi...”
“Of course, by then the culprit had long since slipped out of the room.{r}{p}After rigging the window to break on its own.”
“Break on its own?
What kind of rig?”
Pressed by {n2}, I fell into thought.
What kind of rig could it be?
Snow.
Couldn't something be done with snow?
Then I remembered being startled by snow falling off the roof, and I understood everything.
“It's snow.
He used snow.”
“Snow?”
{n2} asked back, puzzled.
“Yes.
Say he went out through one side of an outward-opening window.”
“And the other side is fixed just firmly enough that wind can't move it.”
“Then he lightly hooks a rope, a yard or two long, onto the handle.”
“On the other end of the rope, some kind of flat board...”
“something like the bottom plate of a ski bag, gets tied on.”
{n2}: “So you connect the window and the board with the rope?{r}{p}Then what?”
“Before jumping outside, he shoves that board into the snow piled on the roof.”
“Then after some time, the snow slides off, and the board falls along with it.”
“The window gets yanked hard and slams against the outer wall...
Crash!{r}{p}
Just like that.”
“The board and rope come off the window and get buried under the snow.”
Mr. Kobayashi nodded, impressed.
“I see.
So in the meantime the culprit could go somewhere far away from here and set up an alibi.”
I went on.
“Right.

But as an alibi, that's incomplete.{r}{p}In this weather, how long would it take to reach a place where a proper alibi could be made?{r}{p}It would be hard to predict exactly when the snow would fall,
and besides, we'd all have to remember clearly when the window broke.”
“True...
It would be a plan that relies terribly on coincidence.”
{n2} said.
“I think the culprit made a far more careful plan.{r}{p}One where, no matter when the window broke, he could establish a solid alibi for that time.”
“Is that...
possible?”
Without answering {n2}'s question, I looked around at everyone's faces.
And my eyes stopped on one of them.
“There's a much better way than risking getting stranded in this blizzard.{r}{p}Change your clothes and hairstyle, come back to this inn, and discover the body together with us...
Don't you think
that's better,
Mr. Mikimoto?”
Everyone looked toward Mr. Mikimoto at once.
He didn't so much as flinch as he met my gaze.
I opened my mouth again.
“Mr. Tanaka wore sunglasses the whole time and wouldn't talk to anyone.{r}{p}If he took off the sunglasses, changed clothes and put on a fake beard, none of us could possibly tell it was Mr. Tanaka.”
With everyone watching, Mr. Mikimoto burst out laughing.
“Then I'd be like the Fiend with Twenty Faces.{r}{p}A master of impossible crimes and disguise, am I?”
“You don't need to be a master of disguise to manage that.{r}{p}None of us knows what Mr. Tanaka really looked like.”
“Fine, let's say that's true.{r}{p}Why can you say this Tanaka fellow is me?”
“By elimination.{r}{p}Everyone except you was at this inn while Mr. Tanaka was here.{r}{p}But since you arrived, Mr. Tanaka hasn't been seen once.”
“Come on.
That doesn't make me him, does it?{r}{p}The culprit could still be out there trudging through the snow right now.”
“That's true.
If that beard of yours is real, I'll withdraw this deduction.{r}{p}You won't mind if I check, right?”
Mr. Mikimoto glared back at me, openly angry.
“Hey,
enough with the jokes.{r}{p}You think this is a fake beard?”
He stood, brought his face close to me, and tugged at his bushy beard with his own hand to show me.
...Had my deduction been wrong?
I hesitated for a moment, then reached out, grabbed Mr. Mikimoto's beard, and pulled hard.
“Ow!”
I ignored his protest and pulled harder.
With an ugly ripping sound, the beard peeled right off.
I thought I'd torn the skin off, but of course I hadn't.
A smooth chin was plainly visible.
“I knew it...”
Before I could even say it, Mr. Mikimoto had grabbed my arm and twisted it behind my back in an instant.
“Owwwww!”
I cried out without meaning to.
Mr. Mikimoto really was the same person as Mr. Tanaka.
He spoke from behind me.
“Didn't think I'd get found out this easily.{r}{p}You're sharper than you look.”
The sound of the fake beard being torn off echoed behind my head, and everyone gasped.
“Then...
then it really was you...?”
Mr. Kobayashi began to say and fell silent.
“That's right.

Just like the kid said.{r}{p}I carried the body into that room.{r}{p}I thought there was no way anyone would see through it.{r}{p}Who'd have thought there'd be a great detective in a place like this.”
I struggled to shake free, but he only twisted my arm tighter.
“Thrash around and it'll snap.”
Threatened in a low voice, I shuddered.
I knew he really could do it, and that he meant it.
“...What are you going to do?”
{n2} said, her face pale.
“Well, now, what to do.{r}{p}Now that it's come to this, we can't exactly all get along until morning.{r}{p}Take a hostage and run, or have every one of you die.”
At his calm tone, I felt the blood drain from my face.
“You may be used to fighting, but you don't think you can beat all of us, do you?”
Toshio said as if challenging him, and Mikimoto... Mr. Mikimoto...
I should stop with the 'Mr.' already.
Mikimoto smirked boldly.
“If you don't mind this kid's arm getting broken, come and get me.”
“Toshio,
do as he says for now.”
I said, sweating.
“Looks like he doesn't like having his arm broken after all.{r}{p}So what'll it be, pal?”
Glaring at Mikimoto with hatred, Toshio kept his hands to himself.
Toshio must have understood that it wasn't a mere threat and he meant it.
Seeing Toshio tremble with rage, I felt a pang of guilt for a moment.
But who could resist when threatened with a broken arm?
“{n1}, you coward!{r}{p}Who cares about an arm!{r}{p}
That guy might kill everyone!”
{n2}'s voice stabbed me right in the chest.
An arm is nothing...
An arm is nothing...
I repeated those words in my head like a spell.
{n2} was in danger too.
I couldn't let him do as he pleased here.
I shouted.
“Toshio!{r}{p}
Hurry and subdue him!{r}{p}Don't worry about me!”
“Don't mind me, subdue him!”
I shouted.
“Oh, is that so.
Looks like you don't know how much it hurts when a bone breaks.”
Mikimoto let out a soft chuckle.
“Life's all about learning.
Let me teach you one thing.”
Instantly, a violent shock ran through my twisted right arm, right between the wrist and the elbow.
“Uwaaaaaaaah!”
I screamed, writhed, broke free of Mikimoto's hands, and crumpled.
My right arm had grown an extra joint, like the leg of some unknown animal.
My wrist dangled and swung.
Nausea and dizziness hit me at once.
I desperately fought to keep from passing out.
Are you okay?”
From about a light-year away, I faintly heard {n2} calling.
“He's fine.
He won't die.{r}{p}Now you understand how much a broken bone hurts.{r}{p}Well, you've got another arm.
Want that one broken too?”
I couldn't believe my ears.
This pain alone was enough to drive me mad, and he was going to break the other one too?
I noticed tears streaming down my face from the pain and frustration, and it made me furious.
To cry in front of a guy like this, a guy like this.
“I won't let you do that!”
I heard {n2} shout.
And the sound of bodies colliding.
I raised my face without wiping my tears, and through the blur I saw {n2} and Mikimoto grappling.
Even blurred, it was plain that {n2}'s body was far too weak to stand up to Mikimoto's huge frame.
Shouting wildly, I slammed my body into Mikimoto's back.
“Waaaaaaaah!”
The instant I hit him, lightning-like pain shot from my arm to my shoulder and from my shoulder to the top of my head, and I nearly fell over from that alone.
I desperately held my ground and glared at Mikimoto, who was staring at me with a look of shock.
“You...
ugh!”
Mikimoto groaned.
The moment his attention wandered, {n2} had kicked him as hard as she could in the groin.
When {n2} pulled away, Toshio leaped in and punched Mikimoto in the face.
He was still standing.
Mr. Kobayashi quietly slipped behind him and wrapped both arms around Mikimoto's neck.
Mr. Kayama and several of the women also jumped in.
The sounds of scuffling, shouting, things breaking...
Before I knew it, even that commotion sounded like a pleasant lullaby to my ears.
Closing my eyes and collapsing to the floor, I slipped smoothly into unconsciousness...
When I came to, I was lying in bed.
Maybe someone had called a doctor; my right arm was now wrapped in a heavy cast.
In the next bed, {n2} was sleeping with her arms as a pillow.
Gradually I began to remember what had happened before I lost consciousness.
...What had happened after that?
I would have to ask her when she woke up, but it also felt like it hardly mattered.
{n2} stirred.
I felt like she had said my name.
I noticed dried traces of tears on her profile.
...Had she cried because she was worried about me?
And had she stayed by my side the whole time?
When she woke up, there'd be so much I wanted to ask and so much I wanted to tell her...
That's what I thought.
A day wouldn't be enough; no, not even a week or a month.
But for now, I'd already decided on the first words.
{n2} slowly raised her face and rubbed her eyes.
I said.
“Good morning,
I felt frustrated that I could do nothing with my broken arm.
But in the next instant, {n2} spun around like a ballet dancer, and Mikimoto flew high into the air.
It was like watching slow motion.
In the next moment, he landed on his back right in the middle of the table.
Broken cups scattered everywhere.
Only when I saw Mikimoto out cold with his eyes rolled back did I realize {n2} had thrown him.
For a while nobody could say a word; everyone stood frozen as if someone had hit pause.
{n2} herself looked surprised too.
She turned to me, a little embarrassed, and said:
“For self-defense,
I study aikido.{r}{p}I didn't think it would go this smoothly...{@}
...{r}{p}I guess he let his guard down because he thought I was a girl.”
As if those words were a signal, everyone hurriedly started moving.
The idea was to tie him up while he was unconscious.
Mr. Kobayashi brought a laundry rope, and Toshio tied up Mikimoto's body and rolled him onto the floor.
{n2} and Mrs. Kobayashi put a splint on my broken arm and gave me first aid.
Relieved, everyone's tension seemed to snap, and they flopped down on the sofas.
“But {n2},
that was amazing, that shoulder throw.{r}{p}I still can't believe a body that big flew through the air.”
When Mr. Kobayashi said that, everyone nodded in admiration.
My deduction seemed to have faded in the shadow of {n2}'s heroics.
This should have been the part where I wowed everyone by explaining in detail how I saw through the trick and when I first suspected Mikimoto.
I felt just a little bitter.

Everyone was safe, after all.

hurt?”
{n2} asked, worried.
yeah.
Kind of...”

cool, you know.”

a charm.”

Her lips touched mine like a feather drifting down.
“...How's that?”
Even when she asked, I couldn't speak for a while.
It seems
it doesn't hurt anymore.”
It was true.
I didn't mind the pain in my arm at all.
Even the bloody case stopped mattering.{g}

it's starting to hurt again.
Could you cast
that charm one more time?”

Midori, astonished, looked down at the cat at her feet.

“Huh...
The lock?{r}{p}W-
well, you're right.
How did she get out, I wonder...”

Oh, yeah...
I guess.
